content.value_statement: Medical device teams need clear regulatory paths across FDA and EU requirements. This skill helps plan submissions, assess risks, and coordinate documentation.
actual_capabilities: Explains FDA 510(k), PMA, and De Novo submission pathways from the included FDA guide.
Explains EU MDR classification, technical documentation, clinical evidence, UDI, and review timelines.
Provides a regulatory decision framework for impact assessment, stakeholder alignment, planning, and review.
Defines cross-functional coordination routines, handoff expectations, and regulatory performance indicators.
Includes a local Python tracker for submission status, approval dates, overdue items, and status reports.
Supports regulatory risk assessment and mitigation planning across the product lifecycle.
limitations: It does not provide legal advice or replace qualified regulatory counsel.
It cannot submit documents to FDA, Notified Bodies, or other authorities.
It does not connect to live regulatory databases or authority portals.
Some resources referenced in SKILL.md are not included in the package.

use_cases.title: Choose an Initial Submission Path
use_cases.description: Compare FDA and EU MDR pathways before committing product scope, evidence plans, and launch timing.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Submission Readiness
use_cases.description: Create milestones, owners, meeting routines, and documentation checkpoints for an active medical device submission.

use_cases.title: Prepare Compliance Inputs
use_cases.description: Align design controls, risk management, clinical evidence, labeling, and quality-system documentation for review.

prompt_templates.title: Identify the Pathway
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new device
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me identify likely regulatory pathways for a medical device. The device is [device type], intended for [use], and targeted markets are [markets].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Submission Checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for FDA or EU MDR work
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a submission checklist for [FDA 510(k), PMA, De Novo, or EU MDR]. Include evidence, quality, labeling, and team inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Regulatory Risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Review regulatory risks for [product] at [development stage]. Include market access, clinical evidence, documentation, timeline, and mitigation actions.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Coordination Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a regulatory coordination plan for [submission type]. Include stakeholders, milestones, handoffs, escalation points, KPIs, and review cadence.

output_examples.input: Plan a 510(k) path for a wearable cardiac monitor.
output: Likely pathway: FDA 510(k), subject to classification and predicate confirmation.
Core evidence: performance testing, software documentation, cybersecurity, labeling, and usability inputs.
Team inputs: engineering, clinical, quality, regulatory, and product owners.
Next step: confirm predicates and request a pre-submission meeting if uncertainty remains.

output_examples.input: Prepare an EU MDR readiness review for a Class IIa device.
output: Review areas: classification, technical documentation, clinical evidence, UDI, QMS readiness, and Notified Body engagement.
Timeline focus: pre-submission preparation, review questions, audit readiness, and post-market obligations.
Risk focus: clinical evidence gaps, documentation traceability, and late Notified Body engagement.

output_examples.input: Create a regulatory meeting cadence for a submission team.
output: Weekly: track open submission actions, blockers, and authority questions.
Monthly: review milestones, risks, resourcing, and executive decisions.
Quarterly: refresh regulatory training and review process improvements.

best_practices: Start pathway analysis before design decisions become difficult to change.
Validate assumptions with current authority guidance and qualified experts.
Keep traceable evidence, decisions, and ownership records throughout development.
anti_patterns: Starting regulatory planning only after product development is nearly complete.
Treating FDA and EU MDR documentation as identical submission packages.
Using the local tracker as the only source of regulated submission records.

faq.question: Which regulatory areas does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers FDA medical device pathways, EU MDR planning, regulatory risk management, submission coordination, and local status tracking.

faq.question: Can it replace a regulatory consultant?
faq.answer: No. It supports planning and preparation, but qualified experts should review specific submissions and legal obligations.

faq.question: Does it submit documents to regulators?
faq.answer: No. It helps organize strategy and documentation, but users must submit through official authority channels.

faq.question: Does it use live regulatory data?
faq.answer: No. It uses included reference material and user-provided context, so users should verify current guidance.

faq.question: What does the tracker script do?
faq.answer: It stores local submission records, updates statuses, identifies overdue submissions, and generates a text status report.

faq.question: Why are some referenced resources unavailable?
faq.answer: SKILL.md names several extra guides and template folders that are not present in this package version.
